_readme: Machine-readable schema for the social-crm-template Airtable base. An agent (or a human) can recreate the full base from this file alone — see SETUP.md for the step-by-step build procedure. Link fields are created in pass 2 (they require the target table to exist first). Every 'multipleRecordLinks' field is defined ONCE, on its owning table; Airtable auto-creates the reverse field on the target table — 'reverseFieldName' is what that auto-created field should be renamed to. Choice lists marked 'personalize' are starter values you are expected to replace with your own.

tables.name: People
tables.description: One record per person. The main contact table.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: Full name or primary identifier

fields.name: Community Name
fields.description: Nickname used in a social scene, club, or community, if any

fields.name: Nicknames / Aliases
fields.description: Common nicknames or alternate names, one per line

fields.name: Instagram / Social
fields.description: Primary social media profile

fields.name: Location
fields.description: Street address or a rough area description

fields.name: Known Since
fields.description: Approximate date first met — use YYYY-01-01 if only the year is known

fields.name: Relationship Tier
fields.description: Building = someone the user is actively turning into a friend (not a friend yet); give Building people a Follow Up Frequency so the bump scan tracks them

fields.name: Follow Up Frequency
fields.description: Per-person reach-out cadence; each choice maps to a day count in SKILL.md — the bump scan computes due-ness from this + Last Contacted

fields.name: Next Follow-Up
fields.description: Optional MANUAL override date for the next planned reach-out; not auto-computed

fields.name: Last Contacted
fields.description: Date of most recent real-world contact; updated when an Interaction is logged

fields.name: Tags
fields.description: Cross-cutting labels. STARTER SET — replace with the contexts of your own life. A 'Local' tag (people geographically near you) is useful for scoping scans

fields.name: Member Status
fields.description: Membership standing in your primary scene/club/community, if you have one. Rename or delete if not applicable

fields.name: Romantic Interest
fields.description: See SKILL.md for the meaning of each stage

fields.name: Likes & Interests
fields.description: Hobbies, preferences, food likes/dislikes, music taste, teams

fields.name: Family and Pets
fields.description: People close to them who don't have their own record. One relation per line as 'Relation: Name'; use '(name unknown)' where a name is not known

fields.name: Job/Employer
fields.description: Job title and/or employer

fields.name: How We Met
fields.description: Brief context for where/how the user met this person

fields.name: History
fields.description: Longer-arc relationship backstory that doesn't fit a single interaction

fields.name: Notes
fields.description: Catch-all, LAST RESORT. If data belongs in a structured field, it goes there instead

fields.name: Partner
fields.description: Their partner/spouse, when that person has their own record. Self-link; Airtable creates a second reverse field — rename it 'Partner Of' or hide it

fields.name: Groups
fields.description: Clubs/groups this person belongs to. Always a linked record, never text in Notes

tables.name: Groups
tables.description: Clubs, teams, communities, friend groups, workplaces.

fields.name: Group Subtype
fields.description: Free-text refinement, e.g. Book Club, Running Club

fields.name: Abbreviation
fields.description: Short form the user actually says, so lookups match casual speech

fields.name: Last Contacted
fields.description: Last time the user showed up to this group

tables.name: Events
tables.description: Parties, trips, gatherings the user attended or hosted. An Event can anchor a Roster and links the People who were there.

fields.name: People
fields.description: CRM contacts who were at this event

tables.name: Interactions
tables.description: Only log an Interaction record when the user explicitly reports having real-world contact with a person who is already in the People table (a text, call, in-person meeting, email). Do NOT create Interaction records when adding a new contact — use the Changelog for that. The Changelog covers additions; Interactions cover actual contact events.

fields.name: Summary
fields.description: One-line description of the contact event

fields.name: Location
fields.description: Where it happened, for in-person contact

fields.name: Notes
fields.description: Longer detail beyond the Summary line

fields.name: Person
fields.description: Who the interaction was with

tables.name: Rosters
tables.description: Name-dump records ('globs'). One record = one list of names from an event, sign-up list, or social circle, kept as TEXT — not contacts. INTAKE RULE: when the user says 'glob this' or dumps a name list, create ONE Rosters record; do NOT create People records or Interactions for the names. Link at least one anchor: Anchor Group, Anchor Person, and/or Event. Names field: one name per line, optional note after ' — '. When a person is later promoted to a real contact, link them in Promoted People on every roster they appear on (keep their name line in Names — it is the historical record).

fields.name: Roster Name
fields.description: Short label naming the source or host, the event, and the date

fields.name: Names
fields.description: The dump. One name per line; optional context note after ' — '. Nicknames welcome

fields.name: Notes
fields.description: Event context, vibes, anything not per-name

fields.name: Anchor Group
fields.description: The club/group touchstone for this roster

fields.name: Anchor Person
fields.description: The friend whose circle this roster came from

fields.name: Event
fields.description: The Events record this roster corresponds to, when one exists. Can be the sole anchor

fields.name: Promoted People
fields.description: Names from this roster that later became real People records — the back-reference

tables.name: Changelog
tables.description: Audit log of changes made to the CRM by the agent. One record per logical change batch.

fields.name: Requested By
fields.description: Who asked for the change (useful when multiple people or automations write to the base)

fields.name: Open Questions / Flags
fields.description: Anything the agent flagged for human review instead of acting on
